title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Overboost Condition
shortDescription: Boost pressure exceeds the maximum allowable threshold for current operating conditions.
fullDescription: Boost pressure exceeds the maximum allowable threshold for current operating conditions.
safetyImpact: Reduced power may impair safe acceleration on highways or merging.

causes.cause: Failed turbocharger or supercharger
Faulty boost pressure sensor
Stuck or seized wastegate
Boost leak in charge pipes or intercooler
Damaged wiring or connector to solenoid/sensor
Carbon buildup in variable-geometry turbo vanes
Failed PCM or boost control module (rare)

symptoms: Whistling or hissing noise from engine bay
Black or blue smoke from exhaust

fixSteps.title: Scan for related codes
fixSteps.instruction: Use an OBD-II scanner to read all stored codes and freeze frame data. Note any companion turbo or boost codes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect boost system for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Visually check all charge pipes, intercooler hoses, and clamps for cracks, oil residue, or loose connections. Smoke-test if available.

fixSteps.title: Test boost pressure sensor and solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe the sensor connector and measure voltage with key-on engine-off and during a road test. Check solenoid resistance against spec.

fixSteps.title: Inspect turbocharger and wastegate
fixSteps.instruction: Check turbo shaft play, wastegate actuator movement, and VGT vane operation. Replace worn components or carbon-clean as needed.

faq.q: Can I drive with a turbo boost code?
faq.a: Most vehicles will enter limp mode and limit power. You can drive short distances at reduced load to a shop, but prolonged driving risks turbo or engine damage.

faq.q: How much does turbo repair cost?
faq.a: Sensor or solenoid replacement is typically $150-$400. A full turbocharger replacement ranges from $1,500 to $4,000 depending on vehicle.

faq.q: What causes overboost vs underboost?
faq.a: Overboost usually means a stuck wastegate or failed boost control. Underboost typically results from a leak, failed turbo, or stuck-open wastegate.
